						<p>Each year, Penguin Random House Education hosts two scholarship essay contests for high school students: The <a href="https://www.penguinrandomhouse.com/signet-essay-contest/" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Signet Classics Essay Contest</a> and the <a href="https://www.penguinrandomhouse.com/pcessay/" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Penguin Classics Essay Contest</a>.</p>
<p>The <strong>Signet Classics Scholarship Essay Contest</strong>, established in 1996, is open to qualifying high school <strong>juniors</strong> and <strong>seniors</strong>. In 2018-2019, students were asked to respond to <a href="https://randomhouse.app.box.com/file/499205743529">questions</a> about <a href="https://penguinrandomhousesecondaryeducation.com/book/?isbn=9780451530943"><em>The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn</em></a> by <a href="https://penguinrandomhousesecondaryeducation.com/author/?authorid=31611">Mark Twain</a>.</p>
<p>Click through to read the winning essays of the five Grand Prize Winners of the Twenty-Third Annual Signet Classics Scholarship Essay Contest:</p>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://www.penguinrandomhouse.com/signet-essay-contest-winner-2019-samuel-freiberger/" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Samuel Freiberger </a>– Samuel completed 12<sup>th</sup> grade at Cathedral School, Natchez, MS.</li>
</ul>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://www.penguinrandomhouse.com/signet-essay-contest-winner-2019-elijah-holton/" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Elijah Holton – </a>Elijah is in the 12<sup>th</sup> grade at San Luis Obispo High School, San Luis Obispo, CA.</li>
</ul>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://www.penguinrandomhouse.com/signet-essay-contest-winner-2019-victoria-lu/" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Victoria Lu – </a>Victoria is in the 12<sup>th</sup> grade at South Side High School, Rockville Centre, NY.</li>
</ul>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://www.penguinrandomhouse.com/signet-essay-contest-winner-2019-tatum-mckenna/" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Tatum McKenna – </a>Tatum completed the 12<sup>th</sup> grade as a homeschool student in Houston, TX.</li>
</ul>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://www.penguinrandomhouse.com/signet-essay-contest-winner-2019-kennon-walton/" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Kennon Walton – </a>Kennon is in the 12<sup>th</sup> grade at University School, Hunting Valley, OH.</li>
</ul>
<p> </p>
<p>The more recently established <strong>Penguin Classics Essay Contest</strong> is open to qualifying high school <strong>freshmen</strong> and <strong>sophomores</strong>. In 2018-2019, students were asked to respond to <a href="https://randomhouse.app.box.com/file/511497932525" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">questions</a> about <a href="https://penguinrandomhousesecondaryeducation.com/book/?isbn=9780142437339"><em>The Crucible </em></a>by <a href="https://penguinrandomhousesecondaryeducation.com/author/?authorid=20634">Arthur Miller</a>.</p>
<p>Click through to read the winning essays of the five Grand Prize Winners of the Third Annual Penguin Classics Scholarship Essay Contest:</p>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://www.penguinrandomhouse.com/penguin-essay-contest-winner-15/" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Charlotte Brown </a> – Charlotte is in the 11th grade at Wasilla High School in Wasilla, AK.</li>
</ul>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://www.penguinrandomhouse.com/penguin-essay-contest-winner-14/" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Molly Cline – </a>Molly is an 11th grade home-schooled student in Stone Mountain, GA.</li>
</ul>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://www.penguinrandomhouse.com/penguin-essay-contest-winner-13/" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Micah Cook – </a>Micah is in the 11th grade at Calvary Christian High School in Clearwater, FL.</li>
</ul>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://www.penguinrandomhouse.com/penguin-essay-contest-winner-12/" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Grace Cuddihy – </a>Grace is in the 10th grade at Avenues in New York, NY.</li>
</ul>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://www.penguinrandomhouse.com/penguin-essay-contest-winner-11/" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Anya Gorgas – </a>Anya is in the 10th grade at Hudson High School in Hudson, FL.</li>
</ul>
<p>Congratulations to all winning ten students for their hard work—Penguin Random House Education is proud to support their academic success and the schools and teachers who make that success possible. Each winner has been awarded a <strong>$1,000 scholarship</strong> and a <strong>Signet Classics or a Penguin Classics Deluxe Library</strong> for their school or local public library.</p>
<p>We’re already looking forward to the 2019-2020 contests. English teachers are welcome to sponsor two students in each contest. Students entering the Signet Classics Scholarship Essay Contest (11<sup>th</sup> and 12<sup>th</sup> graders) will read <a href="https://penguinrandomhousesecondaryeducation.com/book/?isbn=9780451531797"><em>Wuthering Heights </em></a>, and students entering the Penguin Classics Scholarship Essay Contest will read <a href="https://penguinrandomhousesecondaryeducation.com/book/?isbn=9780143104919"><em>Ceremony </em></a>.</p>
<p>For the complete rules and instructions on how to enter the 2019-2020 contests, visit the pages below. Please take a moment to visit our FAQ pages for each contest, and reach out to <a href="mailto:EssayContest@PenguinRandomHouse.com">EssayContest@PenguinRandomHouse.com</a> with any questions.</p>

</ul>

															Emily Brontë’s only novel and a gothic classic—a gripping story of obsession, revenge, and tragedy—now the feature film “Wuthering Heights” from Emerald Fennell, which captures the spirit of this epic love story and stars Margot Robbie as Cathy and Jacob Elordi as Heathcliff.“Whatever our souls are made out of, his and mine are the same.”There are few more convincing, less sentimental accounts of passionate love than Wuthering Heights. 															A haunting examination of groupthink and mass hysteria in a rural communityA Penguin Classic   "I believe that the reader will discover here the essential nature of one of the strangest and most awful chapters in human history," Arthur Miller wrote in an introduction to The Crucible, his classic play about the witch-hunts and trials in seventeenth-century Salem, Massachusetts. Based on historical people and real events, Miller's drama is a searing portrait of a community engulfed by hysteria.   In the rigid theocracy of Salem, rumors that women are practicing witchcraft galvanize the town's most basic fears and suspicions; and when a young girl accuses Elizabeth Proctor of being a witch, self-righteous church leaders and townspeople insist that Elizabeth be brought to trial. The ruthlessness of the prosecutors and the eagerness of neighbor to testify against neighbor brilliantly illuminate the destructive power of socially sanctioned violence.   Written in 1953, The Crucible is a mirror Miller uses to reflect the anti-communist hysteria inspired by Senator Joseph McCarthy's "witch-hunts" in the United States. Within the text itself, Miller contemplates the parallels, writing: "Political opposition...is given an inhumane overlay, which then justifies the abrogation of all normally applied customs of civilized behavior. A political policy is equated with moral right, and opposition to it with diabolical malevolence."
